summary:
KAM ASTRA is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring and intelligent support system designed for long-duration space missions.

It combines biomedical and environmental sensor data with artificial intelligence to monitor vital signs, identify unusual changes, and detect potential health risks early. By comparing measurements with each astronaut's personal health baseline, it provides more personalized monitoring.

Beyond health monitoring, KAM ASTRA features an intelligent AI companion called KAM. It supports natural conversations, motivational interactions, internet research, live information retrieval, image analysis, and visual object recognition. It can communicate with astronauts, provide informational support, analyze visual content, and help reduce the psychological challenges of isolation during long missions.

KAM provides proactive voice alerts and explains health-related changes in natural language. Core health monitoring, risk analysis, local voice alerts, and object recognition are designed to function without an internet connection.

The current working software prototype has been tested through 12 simulation scenarios and 113 automated software tests using simulated data.

KAM ASTRA aims to make space missions safer by combining health monitoring, intelligent assistance, human interaction, and autonomous support technologies.
details:
1. Project Overview and How It Works

KAM ASTRA is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring and intelligent assistance system designed for long-duration space missions. It combines biomedical data, environmental monitoring, artificial intelligence, and human-machine interaction in a single platform.

The system is designed to collect data from biomedical sensors integrated into an astronaut's body surface or spacesuit. These measurements include heart rate, ECG, heart rate variability (HRV), respiration, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), skin temperature, movement, and posture. Environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity, pressure, air quality, and radiation exposure are also considered.

KAM ASTRA processes incoming data, checks its reliability, stores measurements in a local database, and compares the astronaut's current condition with their personal health baseline from the previous 30 days. A rule-based risk engine identifies abnormal changes and assigns risk levels from 0 to 4. Artificial intelligence explains verified findings in natural language and provides proactive voice alerts.

2. Intelligent AI Companion – KAM

One of the most important features of the project is KAM, the intelligent AI companion.

KAM is designed to act as a digital teammate rather than simply a health monitoring interface. Its capabilities include:

  • Natural conversation: Astronauts can communicate with KAM through voice and ask questions naturally.
  • Motivational support: Provides encouraging conversations and emotional support to help astronauts cope with isolation and confinement.
  • Internet research: Searches for information and helps astronauts access relevant knowledge.
  • Live information retrieval: Retrieves up-to-date information when an internet connection is available.
  • Image analysis: Examines visual content and provides contextual information.
  • Object recognition: Identifies objects through local computer-based visual processing.
  • Health assistance: Explains health reports, monitors recorded measurements, and provides proactive voice notifications.
  • Radiation information: Reports accumulated radiation exposure using available mission radiation data.

3. Offline Capability and Reliability

Space missions may experience communication delays or complete loss of connectivity with Earth. Therefore, KAM ASTRA is designed with offline functionality as a core requirement.

Health data logging, rule-based risk assessment, proactive alerts, alarm management, and Turkish voice notifications currently operate without internet access. Object recognition also runs locally. More advanced conversational AI, internet research, live information retrieval, and image analysis currently require an internet connection.

A fully local language model and data synchronization with Earth are planned future developments.

4. Benefits and Intended Impact

KAM ASTRA aims to improve astronaut safety through early risk detection and personalized health monitoring. Its AI companion also addresses the human challenges of long-duration missions, including isolation, limited communication, and the need for continuous assistance.

The intended impact includes:

  • Early awareness of potential health problems.
  • Personalized health monitoring instead of relying only on universal thresholds.
  • Continuous assistance even during communication interruptions.
  • Reduced psychological burden through conversation and motivational support.
  • Better access to information and visual understanding.
  • Improved support for astronauts and medical teams on Earth.

KAM ASTRA is designed to support medical decision-making, not diagnose diseases or replace healthcare professionals.

5. Technology and Development

The project currently exists as a working software prototype using simulated biomedical and environmental data.

Its software architecture includes:

  • Local database and health data logging.
  • Biomedical data processing.
  • Data quality and reliability assessment.
  • Rule-based risk detection.
  • AI-assisted explanations.
  • Voice interaction and notification systems.
  • Image analysis and local object recognition.
  • Health reports and visual dashboards.

The planned hardware infrastructure includes biomedical sensors, environmental sensors, electronic data acquisition, and analog-to-digital conversion (ADC).

The current prototype has been evaluated using 12 simulation scenarios, five risk levels, and 113 automated software tests. The sensor hardware and space qualification stages have not yet been completed.

6. Creativity and Innovation

KAM ASTRA's main innovation is combining personalized astronaut health monitoring with a conversational AI companion in one integrated system.

Instead of treating health monitoring, psychological support, information retrieval, and visual analysis as separate functions, KAM brings them together in a single intelligent assistant.

Its personal-baseline approach, cloud-independent critical alerts, Turkish voice interaction, multi-indicator risk assessment, and holographic health display concept make it a distinctive approach to future space healthcare.

7. Design Considerations

During development, we considered the unique challenges of space missions:

  • Communication delays and internet interruptions.
  • Astronaut isolation and psychological well-being.
  • Reliability and accuracy of sensor measurements.
  • Individual differences in health conditions.
  • Radiation exposure and environmental hazards.
  • Limited opportunities for immediate medical assistance.
  • Data security, reliability, and system continuity.
  • The importance of distinguishing verified sensor data from simulated or missing information.

Our long-term vision is to develop KAM ASTRA into a reliable, autonomous AI health teammate that can accompany astronauts, support their well-being, and help protect human life during future space exploration.
